title: Testing data structures: invariants, boundary cases and randomized tests (CodeSaathi extension)
learningObjectives: Explain the topic and its C rules.
Trace the example and explain its data or control flow.
Identify edge cases and resource-management requirements.
Apply the concept in a tested C program.

understand.concept: Data-structure tests should verify operation results and invariants after every change. Boundary cases include empty, one-element, full-capacity and repeated insert/delete sequences. Randomized tests can explore many operation sequences when paired with a reference model and reproducible seed.
understand.whyItMatters: State-based testing reveals defects that isolated function examples may miss, especially in circular buffers, linked lists and resizing structures.
understand.analogy: Treat each algorithm or resource as a contract whose invariants must remain true after every operation.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy does not replace C's formal rules for pointers, object lifetime, complexity or library contracts.

explain.narrative:
Data-structure tests should verify operation results and invariants after every change. Boundary cases include empty, one-element, full-capacity and repeated insert/delete sequences. Randomized tests can explore many operation sequences when paired with a reference model and reproducible seed.

State preconditions, invariants, empty and full cases, ownership and failure behaviour before implementation. Compile with warnings and test normal, boundary and failure paths.

examples.title: Focused C example
examples.explanation: The assertion checks the stack invariant after a successful push. A full test suite should also check rejected pushes, pop behaviour and that count never exceeds capacity.

practise.guidedTask: State the stack invariant before and after push and pop.
practise.independentTask: Generate deterministic operation sequences and compare the structure with a simple reference array or model.
hints: Use a fixed random seed when reproducing a failing randomized test.
Assertions can be disabled with NDEBUG; do not rely on them as user-input validation.
Test operation sequences, not only individual calls.

questions.prompt: What should be verified before relying on the implementation?
options: Preconditions, invariants, bounds and failure cases.
Only the name of the algorithm.
Whether one input produced a result.
questions.answer: Preconditions, invariants, bounds and failure cases.
questions.explanation: Correctness depends on maintaining the data structure or algorithm contract.

questions.prompt: Which test strategy is most useful?
options: Test empty, boundary and representative operation sequences.
Assume one successful example proves all cases.
questions.answer: Test empty, boundary and representative operation sequences.
questions.explanation: Targeted tests expose defects ordinary examples can miss.
